kf: **Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS)** is a chronic inflammatory disease of the **hair follicle** in the flexures, not an infection of sweat glands.
Recurrent painful nodules, abscesses, sinus tracts and **rope-like scars** in the axillae, groin, buttocks and under the breasts; **double-ended comedones**.
Diagnosis is clinical: typical lesions, typical sites, recurrence (at least twice in 6 months).
Stop smoking, lose weight, analgesia, topical clindamycin 1%, then a **12-week tetracycline course**; screen for metabolic syndrome and depression.
Refer early for Hurley II–III or failed primary care treatment; biologics (adalimumab, secukinumab) are specialist.

sub: About 1% of people; women about 3× more; starts after puberty, average delay to diagnosis around 7–10 years.
Strong links with **smoking** and **obesity**; a third have a family history.

aet: Follicular occlusion with genetic susceptibility (γ-secretase mutations in familial HS).
Smoking (nicotine promotes follicular plugging), obesity, friction, hormones.
myths: **"It's caused by poor hygiene"**: it is not.
**"Repeated incision and drainage cures it"**: lancing gives brief relief but scars and recurs; treat the disease.
patho_lead: HS starts with a **blocked hair follicle** that ruptures and drives chronic inflammation.

mech.t: Hyperkeratosis plugs the hair follicle infundibulum in apocrine-gland–bearing skin.
The follicle swells and ruptures, spilling keratin and bacteria into the dermis.
Innate immunity (IL-1β, **TNF-α**, **IL-17**) causes painful nodules and abscesses: the targets of biologic drugs.
Repeated inflammation forms epithelialised **sinus tracts**, bridged and **tombstone** comedones, and rope-like scars.
mech.cap: Double-ended (tombstone) comedones and sinus tracts in HS.

mech.t: Hurley I: abscesses without tracts; II: recurrent abscesses with tracts and scars; III: diffuse interconnected tracts.

histo: Not needed for diagnosis. Follicular occlusion, perifolliculitis, abscesses and sinus tracts lined by epithelium.

sub: Tetracyclines are avoided in pregnancy; specialist advice on alternatives (e.g. clindamycin, some biologics).
More common and often more severe in people of African descent; scarring and keloids.

comp: Chronic pain, odour, depression and suicide risk; impaired work and relationships.
SCC in long-standing buttock or perineal disease (rare); associated Crohn's disease, spondyloarthritis, PCOS.
prog: Chronic, relapsing; early treatment and lifestyle change limit scarring. Surgery (deroofing, excision) for persistent tracts.
